Cheval Blanc Courchevel will open two private chalets in December 2026, facing the original Maison in the Jardin Alpin of Courchevel 1850. The two houses can be booked separately or joined into a single retreat of 2,400 square metres.

## Two houses on the slopes

The first chalet has five bedrooms over 900 square metres, including a bedroom designed as a suite. The second has nine bedrooms over 1,500 square metres. It adds a double-height pool lit by natural light, a grand salon with two-metre fireplaces, music and games rooms with Formula One and multi-sport simulators, a dining room and a private wine cellar.

Both chalets share private pools, cinemas, fitness rooms, saunas, hammams and Guerlain massage rooms, with direct access to the ski slopes. Children have their own area, Le Carrousel. A team of 15 majordomes and a private culinary team will look after guests. Prices have not been published.

## Peter Marino and Vik Muniz

The common spaces are by the architect Peter Marino, working with long-standing collaborators. The Brazilian artist Vik Muniz painted the landscape frescoes and designed the dining room setting. The interiors also feature straw marquetry by Lison de Caunes, designs by René Bidet and geometric paintings by Guy de Rougemont.

The opening comes in the first winter of Vincent Billiard as Chief Operating Officer of Cheval Blanc, a role he took on 5 October 2026. The Maison is led by its General Manager, Mathieu Hellec.

## The signal

In the Alps, the most exclusive product is no longer a suite but a private house with palace service. With art-filled chalets around its Maisons, LVMH's hotel arm is competing with the private chalet market on its own ground. Congratulations to the Cheval Blanc Courchevel team on this new chapter.
summary: Cheval Blanc Courchevel will open two private chalets of five and nine bedrooms in December, facing the Maison in Courchevel 1850. Together they form a 2,400-square-metre retreat, with common spaces by Peter Marino and frescoes by Vik Muniz.
